problem:
The table shows the amount of water, in gallons, remaining in a tank t minutes after the tank began draining.
t (minutes): 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10
Water (gallons): 182, 160, 147, 121, 108, 85
Based on a line of best fit for the data, approximately how many minutes after the tank began draining will the tank be empty?

bad.why: Picking two points, computing a slope by formula, writing the line, and solving for zero is hand algebra, and a line through two chosen points is not the line of best fit.
The water drops by a roughly constant amount per minute, so the data are linear; an exponential model never reaches zero and cannot predict when the tank is empty.

algebraFirst.description: Estimates a slope from the first and last points (about -9.7 gallons per minute), writes V = 182 - 9.7t, and solves 182 - 9.7t = 0 by hand.

explanationNotes: Explain that a line of best fit is the one straight line that passes as close as possible to all the data points, and the ~ regression makes Desmos find it and draw it. 'Empty' means 0 gallons, so the answer is where the fitted line crosses the horizontal axis, about t = 19 minutes.
notes: Verified: least-squares m = -9.5286, b = 181.476, x-intercept 19.05 (numpy and Desmos v1.11.4, which labels the zero of the regression line itself). A two-endpoint line gives about 18.8, so every reasonable line still picks 19.
